references.text: The children of Reuben and Gad were originally allotted land east of the Jordan, creating a geographical boundary between them and the other tribes.
The Jordan as a boundary between the tribes east and west of the river is a central theme in the allocation of the land.
Moses instructed Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh regarding their inheritance east of the Jordan.
The context for the concern that future generations would be rejected from worshipping the Lord.
The altar was to serve as a witness that the tribes east of the Jordan also had a share in the Lord.
The Levites had no inheritance because the priesthood of the Lord was their inheritance - parallel to the theme of having a share in the Lord.
Levi had no inheritance because the Lord himself was their inheritance - similar language about having a share in the Lord.
